title: Double-Mindedness
english: The cornerstone of our faith is honorable, and those who believe in him will not be put to shame, as it is written in Scripture (1 Peter 2:6).
Paul, our divine messenger, understood this concept very well, and as a wise master builder, he laid a foundation, teaching us about the importance of a strong base.
For no one can lay another foundation except the one that is laid, which is Jesus Christ, the foundation of our faith, as stated in 1 Corinthians 3:11.

Therefore, having the Lord Jesus Christ as the foundation and cornerstone of true knowledge of God, we hold fast to our confession, examining our own heart, lest some unbelief escapes our notice, as warned in Hebrews 12:15, and we examine our own heart.
Lest some root of bitterness spring up and cause trouble, according to what is written, and lead us astray from the path of righteousness.

For the evil thing, the incurable disease, seems to be the double-mindedness, which is the most shameful of all things, and those who are in this state do not suffer willingly, and it would not be wrong to say that it is the most shameful of all things.
For it is easy to fall into this weakness, and one can see a house that has fallen from its foundation, easily destroyed, just like a soul that has lost its way.

In the same way, one can see Satan tempting the human soul, if, having abandoned the foundation, that is, Christ, and being double-minded, it is taken captive by deceit, and thus it would be taken captive.
It seems to me that a disciple of Christ should speak correctly and without reproach about such people, that it would have been better for them not to have known the way of truth.
For it has happened to them as in the true Proverb, a dog returns to its own vomit, and a pig, after being washed, returns to wallowing in the mud, as stated in 2 Peter 2:22.

It is utterly disgusting, brothers, to see an unclean dog returning to its own vomit, and similarly, one who has turned back to their former ways will be condemned, and it is a long and ugly thing, and a pig, after being washed, returns to wallowing in the mud, and it is a long and ugly thing.
It is shameful and absurd to speak of those who have turned back to their former ignorance and unbelief, having previously been cured of the disease of unbelief through faith in Christ.

A certain doctor healed the passion using discoveries from his skill, turning it to gentleness, and soothing the worst part of the evil, but who, having fallen into foolishness, would be taken captive, and it would not be wrong to say that it is the most shameful of all things.

Since it is not the earthly body, but the most powerful soul and mind that have been freed from ancient and miserable thoughts, and we have passed through the disease of politics, and we have examined our own heart, and we have passed through the disease of politics.

And will someone, having mixed everything up, appear and speak a cold word from the heart, and what kind of harm will it bring to us to believe in one father and creator of all things, but to distribute honors also to the worldly demons, thrones, powers, and dominions, and to the holy and God-inspired scripture itself?

It is fitting to say again that it is unbelievable and completely without sound, and even dangerous, to attempt to crown with equal and measured honors, and to envy the one who seeks the earthly kingdom, and those who are under his feet, and have bowed their necks to him as a slave.

For it is not the case that ruling all things is a special privilege for those who have obtained it, but rather it seems that some people think that being subordinate to others is harmonious; however, I think no one is in doubt about the fact that true power comes from God.

And if some of those who have been appointed as subjects are well-disposed and genuine, they will be worthy of respect and glory, but if they are disobedient and ill-tempered, they will be ranked among the most hostile, and they will receive the ultimate justice, according to their deeds.

Nevertheless, it is necessary to examine this matter, and to consider the nature of true authority, and I would say that it is a sign of excellent judgment to be able to see clearly that even those who have obtained genuine glory and are testified to through their actions, sometimes have a share of good reputation and the highest honor, not from their own home or from their own authority, but from the voluntary inclination of the ruler.

And the source of all honor and glory is the will of the king, who is the ultimate authority, and those who receive honors are not those who have them naturally, but those who accept them, and are humble enough to recognize their place.

As long as they think correctly about the king's things, they have a stable power and are in good repute, and their position is secure, but if they turn to the opposite, they will no longer be envied, but will fall into misery and extreme evil, and their downfall will be swift.

And if someone were to devise wicked plans and, driven by unbridled madness, were to rebel and, rashly seizing arms and tyrannical pursuits, were to destroy cities and countries, and, having thrown the necessary yoke on some, were to force the glory of the kingdom upon himself, it would be among the sober, not because of this to be honored, but not even with those ruling all will it be arranged, for true power comes from God alone.

Much is needed, in terms of wisdom and discernment, to navigate the complexities of power and authority, and having been done, rather the words of foolishness and the undertakings of the impious would be requested, and very likely, equal and similar punishment.

But let this be said and understood from our own matters, as if written on a tablet, for the sake of clarity and remembrance, and let us consider the divine, beautiful and sharp-sighted, and the queen of all, according to the inherent nature, and her ineffable power and authority.

For there is one Master of all, and Creator, and Lord of all, who is the source of all power and authority, as stated in Colossians 1:16, and since He is good by nature, in order that this might not be known only to Him, but also to others, He brought into being the things that did not exist, and established the order of creation.

And He created a multitude of holy spirits, greater in number, to serve and worship Him, and to carry out His will, and He established the best order for the things that have come into being, and named some Beginning, and Lordship, and Throne, and some Archangels, and Angels, each with their own role and function.

For He thinks nothing else than what He has, well and blamelessly, in every way and always, and has measured out the honor that seems to Him alone to each of the things that have come into being, according to His wisdom and justice.

The multitude of holy angels in heaven is countless, with certain Archai and Exousiai and Thrones established by God, filling the role of a father or teacher to the others, and things were thus, and not otherwise, from the beginning, and the order of creation has been established by God Himself.

When you hear the sacred Scriptures mentioning Dynamis and Thrones and Kyriotetes, do not suppose a multitude of gods is being proclaimed, but rather the various ranks and orders of angels and heavenly beings, and do not be led astray by ignorance, neglecting the doctrines of truth.

As the blessed Paul writes, one God is the creator and Lord of all, and there is no other, as stated in the Scriptures, and myriads of holy angels stand before Him, worshiping and serving Him, and carrying out His will, as part of the heavenly host.

Everything that has come into being through Him bears the yoke of servitude, and is subject to His authority, as the Creator and Lord of all, as stated in Psalm 103:19, and if some have rebelled and been punished, they have fallen.
Having fallen from the highest city, they have led some on earth astray, trying to seize God's glory for themselves, one of whom was the first.

The word of God says, 'A dog returns to its own vomit, and a pig, after being washed, returns to wallowing in the mud' (2 Peter 2:22), and 'It would have been better for them not to have known the way of truth, or having known it, to turn back to what was handed down to them as a holy commandment' (2 Peter 2:21).

title: The Divine Order and Monotheism
english: …Satan; he is not to be considered a god in truth. Rather, there is one nature that rules over all things. All creatures called into being from it are rational creations, possessing an orderly arrangement; they preserve their assigned position, which is their dignity and excellence, as they all worship the Creator.

The prophet Isaiah says, 'I saw the Lord sitting on a high and exalted throne; and seraphim stood around him, each with six wings. With two they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew; and they were crying out to one another, saying, "Holy is the Lord of powers"' (Isaiah 6:1-3). The word 'Sabbath' signifies this. Consider then how the highest powers are both holy and rational—that is, the seraphim, who, having a measured and servile position, surround the divine throne, as if they were performing the liturgical praises in an orderly fashion.

Therefore, I shall ask you, O noble one: for whom is it appropriate to sit upon the high and exalted throne? And for whom is it appropriate to stand and serve? But I think I will certainly say that, being moved by the matter itself: that the sitting signifies the dignity of the lordship, while the servile position signifies the attendance. Running together with the words of Isaiah, we will also find the blessed David: 'For the Lord says, "He has prepared His throne in heaven, and His kingdom shall rule over all"' (Psalm 103:19). Furthermore, He commands those in power, saying: 'Bless the Lord, all His angels, mighty in strength, doing His word, to hear the voice of His words. Bless the Lord, all His powers, His servants, doing His will. Bless the Lord, all His works' (Psalm 103:20-22). Behold, by this, He says the divine throne is established in heaven; and it is necessary for all to praise Him without ceasing, calling them angels, servants, and powers, having imposed upon all the phrase, 'Bless the Lord, all His works.'

Learn then, rather, and avoid the greatest impiety, which is to count the Creator among His own creations and to measure the Master of all with household measures. For to attribute the created to the glory of the Creator is nothing else than to bring the Creator into the order of the creations. Because it is undesirable for Him to be ranked with those that come from Him, and because a severe judgment awaits those who attribute divine glory to unclean demons, you will understand very well from the Mosaic writings; for it is written: 'Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one' (Deuteronomy 6:4). And again: 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him only shall you serve' (Deuteronomy 6:13). He also commands, saying: 'If the Lord your God destroys the nations you are entering to inherit their land, and you destroy them, beware lest you follow their gods after destroying them, saying, "How did these nations serve their gods? I will do likewise." You shall not do so to the Lord your God. For the abominations which the Lord hated, they did to their gods: they even burned their sons and daughters in the fire to their gods' (Deuteronomy 12:30-31). And again: 'If a prophet arises among you, dreaming dreams, and gives you a sign or a wonder, and the sign or the wonder which he tells you comes to pass, saying, "Let us go after other gods, whom you do not know," you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer, for the Lord your God is testing you, to know whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul. You shall follow the Lord your God, and the prophet who speaks to lead you astray will die, for he has spoken to turn you away from the Lord your God' (Deuteronomy 13:1-5). Indeed, death is the penalty for those who do what is most unrighteous, and this exhortation turns the mind of the upright away.

But He who rebukes those falling into such foolishness is clearly, in some way, not tolerating the worship of others, but affirming His own kingdom alone. For He also spoke through the voice of the holy ones: 'I am God, and there is no other righteous and savior except me' (Isaiah 45:21). Therefore, let us not consider anyone else as God, even though they confess Him to be God over all and through all; nor should we distribute the crown of the kingdom to visible creatures or others, lest we be deceived. For we will not diminish God's glory, and if we try to do so, we will rather fall into the pits of destruction.

But perhaps there is still a secret and dark worshiper of the devil and the demons, who is outwardly adorned with the forms of piety, and as far as his words go, he counterfeits the truth. Let us listen, therefore, to the voice of the God-inspired Scripture: 'God is not mocked' (Galatians 6:7). And let us hear also the divine David lamenting and saying: 'Be wise, then, you foolish ones in the people, and you senseless ones, when will you have understanding? He who planted the ear, does he not hear? He who formed the eyes, does he not see? He who disciplines the nations, will he not correct?' (Psalm 90:9-11).

Since God knows and watches over all things concerning us, let us have a faith that is secure and established; and let us cast away the shame of double-mindedness, remembering the words of the blessed Paul: 'Therefore, my brothers, be steadfast and unshakeable, abounding in the work of the Lord' (1 Corinthians 15:58). Let us carry the genuine faith in belief, as offering a spiritual sacrifice to God, saying with a sincere heart: 'Behold, here we are, we will be yours, for the Lord our God is our God.' And again: 'Lord, our God, possess us; Lord, besides you, we know no other; your name we name.'

For it is necessary to believe, for those who would think rightly, that He is the one God who is over all and through all; He is not brought into being by Himself toward being, nor is He received from another; but being and existing always, eternally before all ages and times, He is incorruptible and immortal, an unapproachable light, dwelling in unapproachable light, a source of wisdom and life, and by nature understood and existing as the good, the root of all power; and while He is known to exist, His nature is unknown. For it is necessary to believe that the one coming is a rewarder of those who seek Him (Hebrews 11:6). Do not doubt, human, nor join with those in error through foolish reasoning, lest you dare to speak in a wandering curiosity. But why do I not learn the nature of the one I worship? Away with the unseasonable inquiry regarding the mind and reason that is brought against the ineffable and incomprehensible nature. For what could human reason be to that beauty, so that it might be able to measure it?

Listen to what the prophet Isaiah says, revealing this to you in a mysterious way: 'Who has measured the waters with his hand, and marked off the heavens with a span? Who has weighed the mountains in a balance, and the hills with a pair of scales?' (Isaiah 40:12). Do not be overly concerned with things beyond nature, but approach through faith, knowing that He exists and is present, both aware and disposing of all things; for to go beyond the measures of humanity with a sober mind is not permitted.

Thus Moses also received faith, for God was saying: 'Speak to the sons of Israel, and say to them, "The Lord, the God of your fathers, has sent me to you"' (Exodus 3:15). He inquired, saying: 'Behold, I am going to the sons of Israel, and I will say to them, "The Lord has called you." But they will ask me,' he says, 'What is His name?' and what shall I say to them? …

title: Divine Generation
english: God's response to human inquiry is to reveal his nature and character.
He says, 'You shall tell the sons of Israel that the One who sent me to you is the eternal, uncreated, and unborn God, always in accordance with the nature of the true God.'
This God has a Son who was born from his substance, through whom he made the ages and gives life to all who are capable of living.
He is the fountain of life, and in his light, we see light.
The divine David sings to God, 'You have multiplied your mercy, and the sons of men hope in the shadow of your wings.' (Psalm 36:7-8)
They will be filled with the richness of your house, and you will give them to drink from the river of your delights.
The only-begotten Son of God is an exact character of the Father's substance, having all the beauty of the Father in himself.
He describes the nature of the one who begot him, and he says, 'I am in the Father, and the Father is in me.' (John 14:10-11)
This relationship is not one of physical bodies, but of spiritual unity and co-existence.
The wise John also testifies to this truth, saying, 'The true light, which illuminates every man coming into the world, was.' (John 1:9)
When considering the nature of God, it is essential to transcend the limitations of human understanding and to recognize that the divine nature is beyond all bodily substance.
The mind should depart from bodily things when learning something about God, for the divine nature is not limited by place or subject to the ideas of shapes.
Even when it is said to generate, it does not fall under certain flows or divisions, for the divine nature generates without being divided.
The manner of divine generation is a mystery that surpasses human comprehension, and even the holy angels, who are far superior to us, are unaware of it.
As the blessed Isaiah says, who can describe his generation? (Isaiah 53:8)
The prophet Habakkuk explains it more clearly, but ultimately, it is a truth that is beyond words and beyond the mind.
The peace of Christ that surpasses all mind will guard our hearts.
The virtue of Christ has covered the heavens, and this covering is not just a physical phenomenon, but also a spiritual one, where the minds of men are covered with the virtue of the Son.
This is because the word about Him is greater than the multitude above and the holy orders.
As a result, the birth of Christ is inexpressible to all creation and completely unknowable.
We can only attempt to understand it by following the divine Scriptures, which provide us with a glimpse of the truth, as if we are seeing it as in a mirror and an enigma.
The examples we use to describe the nature of God and the manner of generation are small and insufficient, and we cannot continuously indicate the truth.
However, it is reasonable to think that there is nothing among the things that have happened that is not inferior to the glory of God.

By setting forth a sensible type for the theoretical things, we can ascend to what is incomparably superior, and as much as possible, we think well, according to what is attainable, going towards the beauty of the divine nature.
Those who are intoxicated with their own wine need to wake up, for they are boasting about their own accomplishments and speaking against God's justice, as the prophet David also says.
They are foolishly weaving a web of deceit with their weak reasonings, and in doing so, they are deceiving simple souls and placing them in error and in pits of destruction.
The wisdom they claim to have is not from above, but rather it is earthly, psychic, and demonic.
They attempt to explain the coessentiality of the Son with the Father, but their words are empty and lacking in truth.
For how can the generated be the same as the ungenerated?
There is a great difference between these concepts, and no word can persuade us that the generated is different from the generator.
However, if it is believed that the Son is truly generated, then He will be coessential with the Father.
If the Father has truly begotten the Son, then it is only logical that the Son shares the same nature as the Father.
It is impossible for the Son to be foreign and of a different kind, for this would imply that the divine nature has undergone a change, which is utterly impossible.
The very notion of begetting implies a shared nature, as seen in the human experience where a human being begets another human being.
Each thing that has the power to beget produces something of the same kind and substance, and it is absurd to suggest that a human being could beget a horse or a horse beget a dog.
Given God's greatness, it is only fitting that His Son would be of the same substance as Himself.
The divine nature does not suffer or undergo change, and it is impossible to think or say otherwise.
If God has created all things in the beginning and has made each thing to be of the same substance as Himself, why would He deprive Himself of this same substance?
If it is impossible to conceive of God in this way, then it is also impossible to suggest that the Son is not of the same substance as the Father.

Those who argue that God has not truly begotten the Son must explain the difference between their words and why they seek to undermine the glory of the Son by claiming that He is of a different substance than the Father.
Ultimately, if God has not begotten the Son, then the Son is not begotten at all, and the question should be resolved once and for all.
Let no one be troubled by the difference of words, for we will not accept the arbitrary opinions of certain people who speak from their hearts and not from the mouth of the Lord, as it is written.

Wake up, those intoxicated with their own wine, not knowing things about themselves, boasting to height, speaking against God injustice, as David also says, weaving a spider's web with weak reasonings, deceiving simple souls, placing them in error, and in pits of destruction, the wisdom is not from above, but earthly, psychic, and demonic, what do they say about the Son's coessentiality with the Father, how can the generated be the same as the ungenerated, there is great difference between the words, for the Son is not to be cut off from coessentiality with the Father, no word persuades us that the generated is different from the generator, but if it is believed to be generated in truth, it will be coessential with the generator.
Let no one be troubled by the difference of words, for we will not accept the arbitrary opinions of certain people who speak from their hearts and not from the mouth of the Lord, as it is written.
